---
name: q1_0-wide-vlen-repack-rowparallel
description: "Decision to optimize Q1_0 matmul on wide VLEN (512-2048) via row-parallel Nx1 repack, not the q4_0_8x8 mmla-fold; recorded in opt_roadmap.md F4"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b6b76240-81f4-4da8-b28a-454652dff28c
  modified: 2026-07-28T10:37:21.979Z
---

For wide VLEN (512/1024/2048) the Q1_0 dot kernel's per-32 `vwredsum`
horizontal reduction wastes most lanes and gets relatively worse as VLEN
grows. Fix = repack + ROW-PARALLEL `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like
`ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic` at repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8`
mmla-fold. N weight rows in N lanes; K-reduction becomes a loop-carried
vertical add per lane -> ZERO horizontal reductions.

**Why:** Q1_0 weights are +-1, so the multiply collapses to a conditional
add (`sumi = vsub_vx(sumi,y); sumi = vadd_vx_m(mask,sumi,2*y)` per column,
int16 accum, 32*127<32767 safe). The 8x8 path's vwmul + vnsrl fold tree is
pointless here (no dequant needed, and the fold IS a reduction).

**How to apply:** fix N=64, adapt LMUL to vlenb so fp32 acc is full
(VLEN=2048->m1, 1024->m2, 512->m4). Per-column vlm (128/block) is the main
tuning cost. Full design + inner loop + sub-features F4a-F4d in
`opt_roadmap.md` F4 (working tree, untracked).

**Status 2026-07-22:** F4a + F4b DONE in kernel-lab (untracked):
`repack_q1_0_to_q1_0_64x1`, scalar oracle (bit-exact vs per-row vec_dot),
RVV `gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0` vl512 (i16m2/f32m4) + vl1024 (i16m1/f32m2), scale
expand via integer bit math (premium has no zfh/zvfh). All-VLEN correctness
PASS; asm clean (3-insn column loop, no spills). QEMU proxy shows 0.73x - a
TCG artifact (masked-op/vlm helper cost), NOT real; same trap that buried
F2 (defer-reductions, removed 2026-07-22 by user decision).

**MEASURED 2026-07-23, RTL rdcycle (vsim-demo/q1_0, nr=64 n=512, warm,
ALL PASS both engines):**
- fpga_l3 VLEN=1024: vl256 829 cyc/row -> gemv 125 = **6.6x**
- premium_full VLEN=512: vl256 1044 -> gemv 174 = **6.0x**
- K=51 extrapolation: ~5-6x on the matmul part of the ROI.

**GEMM (F4c) MEASURED 2026-07-23 (same lab, M=4 activations, cyc/dot warm):**
- fpga_l3 1024 (M-tile 4): vl256 838 | gemv x4 127 | gemm **40** = 3.1x over
  gemv, 20.5x over baseline
- premium_full 512 (M-tile 2): vl256 1046 | gemv x4 206 | gemm **109** = 1.9x
  over gemv, 9.6x over baseline
- Key: one vlm feeds the whole M-tile; per extra activation just 2 int vector
  ops + 1 scalar load. M-tile = 4@1024 / 2@512 (f32m4 register budget), zero
  vector spills both. Gain tracks tile width -> prefill wants VLEN=1024.

Engine gotcha: plain `sim_ax45mpv_premium` = NDS_FELEN=0 config = NO vector
FP (every vf* traps illegal; integer vector + scalar FP fine). The right
VLEN=512 engine is `sim_ax45mpv_premium_full` (added to vsim_andesim
config.yaml: premium RTL + ax45mpv_premium_full.cfg, FELEN=32 = fp32-only
vector FP, enough for zve32f; NOT 64 as first recorded) - there ALL vector
FP passes incl. vfwcvt.f.x.v, so the vsext+vfcvt split in the kernel is
optional (kept for portability, ~free).

Engine specs (cfg facts): fpga_l3 = VLEN/DLEN 1024, FELEN 64, L1 32K/32K,
L2 DISABLED, L3 2MB, MMU sv39. premium_full = VLEN/DLEN 512, FELEN 32, L1
64K I$/8K D$, L2 32KB, no L3, ILM 1MB/DLM 32KB, MMU bare. Premium's 8KB D$
< lab warm set (~15KB) -> its warm numbers include L2 traffic; fpga_l3 runs
L1-resident. Both have HVM (vector local memory) at 0x90000000: fpga_l3
8MB/2banks, premium_full 256KB/2banks+8subports.

**premium_max engine (2026-07-23)**: premium RTL re-elaborated with
ELEN=64 + FELEN=64 + PACKED_FP16=yes + D$ 8K->32K (ax45mpv_premium_max.cfg,
config.yaml entry) - builds clean, probe_max (rv64gcv) 15/15 ok incl.
vle64/vadd e64, vfadd f64, vfwcvt.f.f.v f16->f32 zvfh-encoding. So the
premium package is NOT hard-limited to ELEN32; e64/fp16 are config knobs.
Shootout on it (warm cyc/dot): RAM vl256 1045 / gemv 135 / gemm 75
(32K D$ = 1.5x over 8K D$ on gemv; baseline unchanged -> vl256 is not
D$-capacity-bound); HVM identical to premium_full (753/83/54) - HVM still
beats even 32K D$ for the vlm stream.

**HVM A/B MEASURED 2026-07-23** (hvm.h = ace-tq1 malloc_hvm ported
printf-free, CSR 0xFD1 base / 0xFD0[7:0] log2 size; -DQ1_HVM=1 puts ALL
data in HVM; warm cyc/dot): premium_full vl256 1049->753 / gemv 206->83
(2.5x) / gemm 109->54 (2.0x) - 8KB D$ was the bottleneck, best chain 19.4x.
fpga_l3 vl256 840->785 / gemv 126->92 (1.4x) / gemm 40->37 - already
L1-resident, best chain 22.7x. HVM runs are deterministic (rep0==rep1).
premium 256KB fits a 64-row K=51 strip (18KB); fpga_l3 8MB fits the whole
2560x1024 repacked weight (576KB). Kernel FP footprint is only
scale-application (9 ops/block); hot column loop is pure integer - if an
integer-only engine ever matters, swap those 9 for fixed-point dyq
vmacc.vx + 64 scalar FMAs/block (err ~3e-5 < 1e-4 gate).

**ACE co-design (2026-07-20):** user confirmed int8 dot-product HW exists and
wants custom ACE-RVV instructions (COPILOT), not stock xandesvdot. Template =
their TQ1 ACE lab /local/nick/vsim-workspace/vsim-demo/ace-tq1 (unpack.ace:
`v_w_mul_free_macc` multiply-free widening MAC + trit unpack; tq1.c does
unpack -> macc -> ONE vwredsum/block because TQ1 pairs Q8_K 1-scale/256).
Chosen instruction = **A `v_q1_rowdot`**: `{io vrf:4int result, in vrf:int
activation, in vrf:uint signbits}`, per-lane 4-way sign-dot
`result[lane]+=sum_i(bit_i?+act_i:-act_i)`, activation broadcast, weights
1-bit from the Nx1 repack -> lanes=rows, NO reduction. Sign-bit analog of
VD4DOTS, HW = conditional-negate add-tree (no multiplier). Alternatives: C
`v_q1_sign_macc` (2int, single-row, keeps vwredsum), B `v_q1_unpack`+reuse
mul_free_macc (min HW). Full design + .ace sketch + build order in
opt_roadmap.md F6. Open: confirm COPILOT allows 4int in-lane reduce result
(v_q_tq2_unpack suggests yes). Asked user path A/B/C + activation format
2026-07-20; away, defaulting to A + keep per-32 Q8_0.

**F4d DONE 2026-07-24**: ggml wiring merged on llama.cpp branch q1_0-rvv-opt
(block_q1_0x64 + generic + RVV vlenb-dispatch kernels + dispatch gate
Q1_0/riscv_v/VLEN>=512/rows%64; test tests/test-repack-q1_0.cpp, bit-exact
at QEMU 512+1024; e64+zvfh REPACK blockers fixed; ROI counter moved before
extra-dispatch in ggml-cpu.c or repacked matmuls shift K).
**K=51 in-model fpga_l3: 4,476,168 -> 2,144,755 (repack, 2.09x) -> 946,460
(weights-in-HVM, 2.27x over repack, 4.73x over pristine). DONE + committed
2026-07-25** (q1_0-rvv-opt 510479ad8 code, 3aeb5c27a docs). Gap-vs-lab was
memory-bound: K=51 weight = 360KB whole / ~22KB per 64-row strip (NOT
576KB/18KB as older docs said - weight ne=[2560,1024], 1024 rows x 360B);
streamed from L3 (fpga_l3 L1 32K, L2 off).

**weights-in-HVM mechanism**: repack buft = ONE big alloc for all Q1_0 repack
tensors, tensor->data is absolute ptr, kernel reads src0->data -> redirect
per-tensor at load; injection = set_tensor BEFORE ->repack(), point
tensor->data at HVM so repack writes sign-planes straight in (zero copy). QEMU
(machine andes_ae350) backs 0x90000000 as writable RAM (memory_region_init_ram,
hvm_size_pow_2 from -readconfig cfg: fpga_l3 8MiB/23); CSR 0xFD1/0xFD0 discovery
works in guest. Files: ggml-cpu/hvm.h (pure ggml_hvm_bump + ggml_hvm_selected +
target CSR readers), repack.cpp set_tensor redirect (env GGML_Q1_HVM or
-DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v substring; static ggml_hvm_alloc bump 64-align
NULL-on-overflow; 22 attn_v fit 8MB, rest overflow to RAM), ggml-cpu.c ROI
print `[roi] MUL_MAT #K src0=name`, tests/test-hvm-place.cpp (host RED->GREEN),
run-k51-hvm.sh.

**CORRECTNESS bit-exact verified**: HVM-on vs no-HVM binaries (both VLEN 1024
greedy, same prompt) produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output. Verified via a NEW andesim
ability committed 2026-07-25 (andesim branch llamacpp, feat(run) 5f039b5):
`run --mode fast --engine vsim:<eng>` now accepts a vsim engine, probes its
--print-qemu-config (sync_qemu_cfg) and -readconfig's its HVM geometry, so the
whole model runs functionally under HVM with NO cycle leg (minutes, not hours).
Impl: pure helper fast_engine_qemu_extras in driver/run_plan.hpp (tested in
plan_test.cpp), run_fast in driver/cmd_run.cpp.

**GOTCHA (2026-07-25)**: the sshfs toolchain (/local/nick/SW_Release) works
fine; the real blocker was `/tmp` = a tmpfs with a 1M INODE cap, shared
machine-wide and saturated (df shows GBs free but `df -i /tmp` = 100%, ~2 free)
-> gcc temps + Claude harness output ENOSPC, no execve issue. Fix: export
TMPDIR=/home/nick/tmp (ext4, 176M inodes) for all builds + andesim runs.
andesim guest-RAM mmap goes to /dev/shm (also tmpfs) - clean
/dev/shm/hsim-shm.* if it fills. The vlinux exit-trap (mcause=0x2 at
~0x7cffffff, after generation) is GENERIC - base binary traps identically, NOT
HVM-related. premium_max K=51 still BLOCKED: ax45 hybrid resume can't halt hart
(PLDM 0xE6800000 unserved in vsim_andesim ax45 wrapper; ax46 fine).

**F5 SW-prefetch DONE 2026-07-27 (no HVM, user dropped HVM)**: repack gemv
weight stream (bx[l], block_q1_0x64 = 1152B = 18 cache lines (64*18B; the
"2176B/34 lines" in the repack.cpp comment + earlier notes is WRONG), walked
sequentially) is load-bound because this core's HW prefetch is shallow
(NDS_L3C_PFP_LINE_NUM=0, D$ 4 entries). Added __builtin_prefetch of block
l+Q1_PREFETCH_DIST at top of both gemv l-loops in arch/riscv/repack.cpp
(helper q1_prefetch_block). Needs -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON (else __builtin_prefetch
is a nop; gcc14.2 emits real prefetch.r under -march=..._zicbop; added to
build.sh). K=51 fpga_l3 VLEN1024 cycle-accurate: baseline 2,144,213 -> DIST=1
**1,391,650 (1.54x, BEST)** / DIST=2 1,430,534 (1.50x) / DIST=4 1,506,429
(1.42x) -> more lookahead is WORSE (one 18-line block ahead already hides
L3/DRAM latency, further adds MSHR/cache pressure). Default set DIST=1.
Bit-exact (qemu fast: prefetch vs baseline byte-identical text; prefetch.r is
architecturally a no-op hint). UNLIKE HVM (fit only ~1.4% of weights) this
generalizes to ALL Q1_0 matmuls -> broad whole-decode win. vs pristine 3.22x.
Measurement: each K=51 run ~18-40min (RTL leg ~2M cyc at few kHz, machine
shared w/ other users' sim_ax46mpv jobs); cycle count is contention-independent
so ran DIST variants concurrently.
GEMM/prefill ALSO prefetched now (same helper, 4 prefetch.r sites): pure-gemm
node (nrows=4) 1,696,704 -> 1,649,275 = only 1.03x - gemm reuses each weight
block across the M-tile of 4 activations so ~4x less memory-bound than gemv,
little latency to hide. Kept (correct, ~free). So prefetch is a DECODE/gemv win.
METHODOLOGY GOTCHA: K=51 ROI fires in llama.cpp WARMUP pass (nrows=2, pure gemv;
gemm needs nrows>3 per repack.cpp:4400 forward_mul_mat_one_chunk). Use
--no-warmup so #51 = real prefill layer-7 V-proj, nrows=prompt tokens
("The capital of France"=4=pure gemm, "...is"=5=gemm4+gemv1). Added nrows to
the [roi] print (ggml-cpu.c). Docs updated (roadmap F7 + tutorial 5.7).
UNCOMMITTED (harness: commit only when user asks).
ax46mpv_fpga_l3 cache cfg: I$/D$ 32K 4-way 64B line, NO L2, L3 2MB 4-bank
16-way 512b, BIU 512b, VLSU_MSHR 16 / L3_NXACT 16, HVM 8MB@0x90000000.

**F5 ported to kernel-lab 2026-07-28 (uncommitted)**: q1_prefetch_brick +
_nopf twins of both gemv (gemv_..._vl512/_vl1024_nopf, dist folded via an
always_inline _core taking pf_dist) so ONE binary A/Bs purity and cycles on the
same cache state; Makefile PFDIST=n knob + `make check-pf`. Tests: all VLEN
512/1024/256/128 PASS, bit-identical to _nopf at dist 0/1/2/4, checksum
unchanged.
**TRAP (cost a real debug cycle, hit in BOTH lab and ggml)**: a prefetch has no
observable side effect, so the moment GCC 14.2 leaves the prefetch helper out of
line (partial inlining does this) ipa-pure-const marks it pure and DCE deletes
EVERY call - zero prefetch.r in the binary, no warning, and a result-equality
test still passes (a deleted prefetch changes no result). Fix = always_inline on
the helper; ONLY counting prefetch.r in the emitted code catches it.
In ggml this bites at **-Os = CMake MinSizeRel: 0 of 4 sites survive**
(-O1/-O2/-O3 were fine). always_inline added to q1_prefetch_block
2026-07-28; verified the -O3 assembly is BYTE-IDENTICAL with/without the

# kernel-lab: standalone Q1_0 kernel verification

Extracts the Q1_0 x Q8_0 dot kernels out of ggml so one kernel can be built
and verified in isolation, without building llama.cpp.

## Files

- `q1_0.h` / `q1_0.c` - the kernels:
  - `ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0_generic` copied from `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/quants.c:127`
  - `ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0` (+ `_vl256`, `_vl128`) copied from
    `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484` (`static` removed in the lab)
  - F4a: `repack_q1_0_to_q1_0_64x1` (row-major blocks -> column-major 64-row
    bricks) + `gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0_generic` scalar oracle (reference float-op
    order -> bit-exact vs per-row vec_dot on the original data)
  - F4b: `gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0` dispatcher + `_vl512` (i16m2/f32m4, premium)
    and `_vl1024` (i16m1/f32m2, fpga_l3) row-parallel RVV gemv - 3 vector
    ops per column, no reductions, no vector->scalar moves; per-row scales
    expanded fp16->fp32 with integer bit math (no zfh/zvfh, premium-safe)
  - F5: `q1_prefetch_brick` - SW prefetch of the brick `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST`
    blocks ahead (18 cache lines each), copied from `q1_prefetch_block` in
    `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1731`. Each gemv exists twice:
    `_vl512`/`_vl1024` prefetch at the build distance, `_vl512_nopf`/
    `_vl1024_nopf` are the same kernel with the prefetch compiled out, so one
    binary can A/B correctness and cycles on the same cache state
  - fp16 conversion from `ggml/src/ggml-impl.h` (exact, table-free)
  - (the F2 defer-reduction candidates `_vl512`/`_vl512w` lived here until
    2026-07-22; removed - superseded by the F4 row-parallel repack)
- `test_q1_0.c` - correctness harness comparing every kernel vs the scalar
  reference; `test_repack_gemv` gates F4a bit-exact and F4b by the double-ref
  bound. Correctness only - cycles come from vsim (`vsim-demo/q1_0` rdcycle)

## Build and run

```
make host && ./test_q1_0_host            # x86: harness sanity (dispatcher==generic)
./test_q1_0_host --inject                # prove the harness detects a broken kernel
make rv64                                # cross build, static, RVV enabled
../run-rv64-qemu.sh $PWD/test_q1_0_rv64  # QEMU, VLEN=512 (vl256 path)
QEMU_CPU=andes-ax45mpv,vlen=256,zfh=true,zvfh=true ../run-rv64-qemu.sh $PWD/test_q1_0_rv64
QEMU_CPU=andes-ax45mpv,vlen=128,zfh=true,zvfh=true ../run-rv64-qemu.sh $PWD/test_q1_0_rv64  # vl128 path
make asm                                 # q1_0_rv64.s for LMUL/vl inspection
make check-pf                            # F5: prove prefetch.r is really emitted
make clean && make rv64 check-pf PFDIST=2   # sweep the prefetch distance (0 = off)
```

`PFDIST` is not tracked by make, so change it only after `make clean` (or
`touch q1_0.c`), otherwise you re-run the old binary.

QEMU is for correctness only: qemu-user TCG charges a big fixed cost per
vector instruction, scalar instructions are nearly free, and pipeline stalls
do not exist - any timing it reports is misleading. Cycle decisions come from
vsim rdcycle (`/local/nick/vsim-workspace/vsim-demo/q1_0`, copies of these
kernels + mcycle A/B harness) or FPGA.

## What "verified" means

1. **Bit-exact gate**: RVV result == scalar reference result, compared as raw
   float bits, over random + edge data (all-0/all-1 sign bits, q8 saturated
   +-127, zero scales) at sizes 128..8192. The current RVV kernels do the
   same float ops in the same order as the reference, so 0 tolerance applies
   (build uses `-ffp-contract=off` to keep both sides unfused).
2. **Double-reference gate**: |result - double_ref| / sum(|terms|) < 1e-4.
   This is the gate a future optimized kernel must pass when it reorders the
   float accumulation (the F4 row-parallel repack kernels will) and
   bit-exactness vs the reference no longer applies. The per-group integer
   sums must still be exact.
3. **Harness self-test** (`--inject`): flip one weight sign bit, require the
   kernel result to change. A harness that passes a broken kernel is worse
   than no harness.
4. **Cross-platform checksum**: the PRNG is deterministic, so the final
   result checksum must be identical on x86 host and QEMU at every VLEN.
5. **Prefetch is a pure hint** (`test_prefetch_is_pure`): every gemv must
   return rows bit-identical to its `_nopf` twin, at any `PFDIST`, including
   `nb <= dist` where the `t < nb` guard must suppress every prefetch.
6. **Prefetch codegen gate** (`make check-pf`): the optimization can vanish
   with no warning in two ways - `zicbop` missing from `MARCH`, or the helper
   left out of line, because a prefetch has no observable side effect so
   `ipa-pure-const` marks the helper pure and DCE deletes every call. Gate 5
   passes happily either way (a deleted prefetch changes no result), so the
   only real check is counting `prefetch.r` in the emitted code. This is why
   `q1_prefetch_brick` is `always_inline` - measured, not decorative: without
   it GCC 14.2 at -O2 emits zero prefetches here.

## Data domain constraints (match ggml, do not "fix")

- `n % 128 == 0` (QK1_0); the ggml dispatcher guarantees this.
- q8 quants in [-127, 127]: ggml Q8_0 quantization never emits -128.
  The RVV kernel's `vneg` on int8 -128 would wrap to -128 while the scalar
  reference negates in 32-bit; feeding -128 produces a false mismatch.
- No NaN/Inf scales: real quantization never produces them, and NaN payload
  propagation may differ between fp16 conversion implementations.

`touch q1_0.c`), otherwise you re-run the old binary.

QEMU is for correctness only: qemu-user TCG charges a big fixed cost per
vector instruction, scalar instructions are nearly free, and pipeline stalls
do not exist - any timing it reports is misleading. Cycle decisions come from
vsim rdcycle (`/local/nick/vsim-workspace/vsim-demo/q1_0`, copies of these
kernels + mcycle A/B harness) or FPGA.

## What "verified" means

1. **Bit-exact gate**: RVV result == scalar reference result, compared as raw
   float bits, over random + edge data (all-0/all-1 sign bits, q8 saturated
   +-127, zero scales) at sizes 128..8192. The current RVV kernels do the
   same float ops in the same order as the reference, so 0 tolerance applies
   (build uses `-ffp-contract=off` to keep both sides unfused).
2. **Double-reference gate**: |result - double_ref| / sum(|terms|) < 1e-4.
   This is the gate a future optimized kernel must pass when it reorders the
   float accumulation (the F4 row-parallel repack kernels will) and
   bit-exactness vs the reference no longer applies. The per-group integer
   sums must still be exact.
3. **Harness self-test** (`--inject`): flip one weight sign bit, require the
   kernel result to change. A harness that passes a broken kernel is worse
   than no harness.
4. **Cross-platform checksum**: the PRNG is deterministic, so the final
   result checksum must be identical on x86 host and QEMU at every VLEN.
5. **Prefetch is a pure hint** (`test_prefetch_is_pure`): every gemv must
   return rows bit-identical to its `_nopf` twin, at any `PFDIST`, including
   `nb <= dist` where the `t < nb` guard must suppress every prefetch.
6. **Prefetch codegen gate** (`make check-pf`): the optimization can vanish
   with no warning in two ways - `zicbop` missing from `MARCH`, or the helper
   left out of line, because a prefetch has no observable side effect so
   `ipa-pure-const` marks the helper pure and DCE deletes every call. Gate 5
   passes happily either way (a deleted prefetch changes no result), so the
   only real check is counting `prefetch.r` in the emitted code. This is why
   `q1_prefetch_brick` is `always_inline` - measured, not decorative: without
   it GCC 14.2 at -O2 emits zero prefetches here.

## Data domain constraints (match ggml, do not "fix")

- `n % 128 == 0` (QK1_0); the ggml dispatcher guarantees this.
- q8 quants in [-127, 127]: ggml Q8_0 quantization never emits -128.
  The RVV kernel's `vneg` on int8 -128 would wrap to -128 while the scalar
  reference negates in 32-bit; feeding -128 produces a false mismatch.
- No NaN/Inf scales: real quantization never produces them, and NaN payload
  propagation may differ between fp16 conversion implementations.

## 真實 shape (Bonsai-4B, 36 layers, K=ne[0]=reduce dim)

| tensor | K | rows | blk/row | 64-row brick | 整個 tensor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| attn_k, attn_v | 2560 | 1024 | 20 | 22.5 KB | 0.35 MB |
| attn_q | 2560 | 4096 | 20 | 22.5 KB | 1.41 MB |
| attn_output | 4096 | 2560 | 32 | 36.0 KB | 1.41 MB |
| ffn_gate, ffn_up | 2560 | 9728 | 20 | 22.5 KB | 3.34 MB |
| ffn_down | 9728 | 2560 | 76 | 85.5 KB | 3.34 MB |
| token_embd (LM head) | 2560 | 151669 | 20 | - | 52.1 MB |
| **lab 現在** | **512** | **64** | **4** | **4.5 KB** | **4.5 KB** |

只有 3 個不同的 K (2560/4096/9728)，所以 shape sweep 很小。

LM head 沒有走 repack: `repack.cpp:4888` 要求 `ne[1] % 64 == 0`，151669 % 64 = 53。它是 decode 裡最大的一個 matmul (52 MB)，目前完全沒有被優化到。

## 為什麼 shape 會改變 speedup

GEMV 對 weight 沒有任何 reuse - 每個 byte 讀一次。所以決定 speedup 的是「這些 byte 從哪一層 memory 來」。fpga_l3 = L1 D$ 32K / 沒有 L2 / L3 2MB，剛好切出三個區間:

1. lab 現在 4.5 KB - 完全在 L1，warm rep 量到的是純 compute → **6.6x**
2. K=2560 brick 22.5 KB 進得去 L1，整個 tensor 0.35/1.41 MB 進得去 L3 → L3 streaming
3. K=9728 brick 85.5 KB，或整個 tensor 3.34 MB > L3 → DRAM streaming

這就是 lab 6.6x 對 in-model 2.09x 的差距來源，也是 prefetch 能再拿 1.54x 的原因。跑 shape sweep 會直接畫出這條下降曲線。

## Sim 時間 (用實測 1.62 / 0.244 cyc per row*col，RTL ~1.2 kHz)

最小的完整 shape (attn_v) 約 4.9 Mcyc ≈ 68 分；ffn 約 46 Mcyc ≈ 11 小時；LM head 723 Mcyc 不可能。其中 87% 的 cycle 花在 baseline leg。

破解方法: cycles 對 rows 是線性的 (brick group 之間零 reuse)，所以用**真實 K + 截短 rows**。rows=128 (2 個 brick group) 掃 K = {512, 2560, 4096, 9728}，每個 run 約 0.6 Mcyc ≈ 8 分；再用 attn_v 完整 1024 rows 跑一次驗證線性。

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the RISC-V llama-completion binaries for the Q1_0 prefetch reproduce
# runbook (q1_0_hvm_reproduce.md): pristine / baseline / prefetch (+ optional hvm).
#   pristine = upstream kernel, no repack
#   baseline = repack row-parallel kernel, prefetch OFF (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0)
#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   hvm      = repack + weights-in-HVM (older experiment, now superseded)
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh prefetch           # just the shipped kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# The settings that MUST be right (else the guest crashes / baseline is wrong):
#   -static                : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK      : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON    : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                            gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)
#   -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=N   : prefetch lookahead in blocks; 0 = off (baseline), 1 = shipped
#   -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME     : HVM redirect selector; only on the HVM build
cfg() {  # $1 build dir   $2 repack toggle   $3 extra defines (DIST / HVM selector, or "")
  local FL="$3 -mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I $ANDESIM/build/runtime/include"
  cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$1" \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF \
    -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
    -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON \
    -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
    $2 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
  cmake --build "$1" --target llama-completion -j"$(nproc)"
}

build_one() {  # $1 = pristine | baseline | prefetch | hvm
  case "$1" in
    pristine) cfg "$LLAMA/b-pristine" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF" "" ;;
    baseline) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    prefetch) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    hvm)      cfg "$LLAMA/b-hvm"       "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v" ;;
    *) echo "unknown target '$1' (want pristine|baseline|prefetch|hvm)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  cp "$LLAMA/b-$1/bin/llama-completion" "$LLAMA/bin-$1"
  echo "built: $LLAMA/bin-$1"
}

for t in ${*:-pristine baseline prefetch}; do build_one "$t"; done

/* andesim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
